title: Conflict and Congruency Effects in Large Language Models: In-Weight and In-Context Competition in a Verbal Conflict Task
abstract: arXiv:2608.11510v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Congruency effects, observed in conflict tasks such as Stroop and flanker tasks, have been investigated for nearly a century in psychology and neuroscience, but their mechanistic basis is not fully understood. We introduce a verbal-only LLM conflict task in which a prompt stem elicits a default same-color completion and an explicit rule either agrees with (congruent condition) or conflicts with (incongruent condition) the completion. translated_title: 大型语言模型中的冲突与一致性效应：言语冲突任务中的权重内与上下文竞争
translated_abstract: 摘要：在Stroop和侧翼任务等冲突任务中观察到的一致性效应，已在心理学和神经科学领域研究了近一个世纪，但其机制基础尚未完全理解。我们引入了一种仅言语的LLM冲突任务，其中提示词干引发默认的同色补全，而明确规则要么与补全一致（一致性条件），要么与补全冲突（不一致性条件）。Gemma-2-2B和六个参数范围从410M到12B的Pythia模型表现出强烈的默认同色倾向，七个模型中有六个表现出强烈的一致性效应。通过因果归因分析、注意力分析和注意力消融，我们识别出这些LLM中不同的处理路径：一条涉及对表面颜色线索的短程注意力路径，在一致性条件下优先激活；另一条涉及对规则前缀的长程注意力路径，在冲突解决中发挥作用。
tldr: 本文通过言语冲突任务揭示了大型语言模型中存在两种独立处理路径，分别支持一致性条件下的表面线索加工和冲突条件下的规则依赖加工，并系统验证了其机制。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals two distinct processing pathways in large language models—one supporting superficial cue processing in congruent conditions and another supporting rule-dependent processing in conflict conditions—through a verbal conflict task, providing mechanistic insights into congruency effects.
